    Solve 4x2+81=04x^2 + 81 = 04x2+81=0.

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose C: Stops at the fact that no REAL number works, without naming the larger system.

    Isolate the square, then take both square roots of a negative number using −k=ik\sqrt{-k} = i\sqrt{k}−k​=ik​.

    x2=−814⟹x=± i814=±92ix^2 = -\frac{81}{4} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x = \pm\, i\sqrt{\frac{81}{4}} = \pm\frac{9}{2}ix2=−481​⟹x=±i481​​=±29​i

    Both values check: (92i)2=814i2=−814\left(\tfrac{9}{2}i\right)^2 = \tfrac{81}{4}i^2 = -\tfrac{81}{4}(29​i)2=481​i2=−481​.

    What is ∣−11+4i∣|-11 + 4i|∣−11+4i∣?

    Answer choices for question 4

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Stops at the sum of the squares without taking the square root.

    You chose C: Adds the sizes of the two parts instead of using the Pythagorean formula.

    You chose D: Adds the two parts as signed numbers and reports the size of the total.

    Square each part, add, then take the non-negative square root, in that order. Squaring erases the sign of the real part.

    ∣−11+4i∣=(−11)2+42=121+16=137|-11 + 4i| = \sqrt{(-11)^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{121 + 16} = \sqrt{137}∣−11+4i∣=(−11)2+42​=121+16​=137​

    Nothing divides 137137137 into a square, so the exact modulus is the surd itself.

    A single slide of the complex plane carries the point 5+7i5 + 7i5+7i onto the point −1+2i-1 + 2i−1+2i. Which number is being added?

    Answer choices for question 7

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Computes the starting number minus the image, running the slide backwards.

    You chose B: Adds the two numbers instead of subtracting to find the shift.

    You chose C: Subtracts the real parts correctly but takes the imaginary parts in the reverse order.

    Adding www sends zzz to z+wz + wz+w, so www is the image minus the starting number.

    w=(−1+2i)−(5+7i)=(−1−5)+(2−7)i=−6−5iw = (-1 + 2i) - (5 + 7i) = (-1 - 5) + (2 - 7)i = -6 - 5iw=(−1+2i)−(5+7i)=(−1−5)+(2−7)i=−6−5i

    The slide moves every point of the plane 666 units left and 555 units down.

    Solve 2x2+6x+5=02x^2 + 6x + 5 = 02x2+6x+5=0.

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Divides the numerator by aaa rather than by 2a2a2a.

    You chose C: Opens the numerator with +b+b+b instead of −b-b−b.

    You chose D: Divides only the real part of the numerator by 2a2a2a, leaving the imaginary part undivided.

    With a=2a = 2a=2, b=6b = 6b=6, c=5c = 5c=5 the discriminant is 36−40=−436 - 40 = -436−40=−4, so −4=2i\sqrt{-4} = 2i−4​=2i and the whole numerator is divided by 2a=42a = 42a=4.

    x=−6±−44=−6±2i4=−32±12ix = \frac{-6 \pm \sqrt{-4}}{4} = \frac{-6 \pm 2i}{4} = -\frac{3}{2} \pm \frac{1}{2}ix=4−6±−4​​=4−6±2i​=−23​±21​i

    Write 16+3i2+i\dfrac{16 + 3i}{2 + i}2+i16+3i​ in standard form a+bia + bia+bi.

    Answer choices for question 10

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Divides real part by real part and imaginary part by imaginary part.

    You chose C: Uses the conjugate but reads i2i^2i2 as +1+1+1 in the numerator, giving 292929 rather than 353535.

    You chose D: Multiplies top and bottom by the denominator itself, so an iii survives downstairs.

    Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, which is multiplying by 111. The new denominator is the real number 22+12=52^2 + 1^2 = 522+12=5.

    16+3i2+i=(16+3i)(2−i)5=32−16i+6i+35=35−10i5=7−2i\frac{16 + 3i}{2 + i} = \frac{(16 + 3i)(2 - i)}{5} = \frac{32 - 16i + 6i + 3}{5} = \frac{35 - 10i}{5} = 7 - 2i2+i16+3i​=5(16+3i)(2−i)​=532−16i+6i+3​=535−10i​=7−2i

    Check by multiplying back: (7−2i)(2+i)=14+7i−4i+2=16+3i(7 - 2i)(2 + i) = 14 + 7i - 4i + 2 = 16 + 3i(7−2i)(2+i)=14+7i−4i+2=16+3i.

    Solution

    Solution

    You chose B: Takes the product of the pair as a2−b2=64−9a^2 - b^2 = 64 - 9a2−b2=64−9.

  13. 13

    Let ax2+bx+cax^2 + bx + cax2+bx+c have real coefficients with a≠0a \ne 0a=0. Now that the complex numbers are available, what does the sign of b2−4acb^2 - 4acb2−4ac decide?

    Answer choices for question 13

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Keeps the discriminant in its old job of counting, when the count is now always two with multiplicity.

    You chose C: Over the complex numbers every quadratic splits into two linear factors, whatever the sign.

    You chose D: Fails on x2−4x^2 - 4x2−4, whose discriminant is positive while its roots ±2\pm 2±2 are equally far from 000.

    Over the complex numbers a quadratic always has two roots counted with multiplicity, so the discriminant no longer settles how many roots there are. What it reports now is position: a negative value sends the pair off the real axis, symmetrically about it, while its vanishing is what makes the two coincide.

    b2−4ac<0⟹x=−b2a±4ac−b22a ib^2 - 4ac < 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x = -\frac{b}{2a} \pm \frac{\sqrt{4ac - b^2}}{2a}\,ib2−4ac<0⟹x=−2ab​±2a4ac−b2​​i

    The shared real part is the axis of symmetry, and the opposite imaginary parts place one root above the axis and one below.

    The number zzz lies in Quadrant IV of the complex plane. Where does −z‾-\overline{z}−z lie?

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Reflects across the real axis and stops, never applying the minus sign.

    You chose B: Negates zzz itself rather than its conjugate, which moves the point through 000.

    You chose D: Treats the reflection and the minus sign as undoing each other, leaving the point where it was.

    In Quadrant IV the real part is positive and the imaginary part is negative, so write z=a+biz = a + biz=a+bi with a>0a > 0a>0 and b<0b < 0b<0. Conjugating flips the sign of bbb only, and the minus sign then flips both parts.

    −z‾=−(a−bi)=−a+bi-\overline{z} = -(a - bi) = -a + bi−z=−(a−bi)=−a+bi

    Now −a<0-a < 0−a<0 and b<0b < 0b<0, which is Quadrant III.

    The real numbers xxx and yyy satisfy (x+yi)(1+i)=5−i(x + yi)(1 + i) = 5 - i(x+yi)(1+i)=5−i. What are they?

    Answer choices for question 15

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Matches the expanded parts the wrong way round, solving x+y=5x + y = 5x+y=5 and x−y=−1x - y = -1x−y=−1.

    You chose C: Divides part by part, reading off 5÷15 \div 15÷1 and −1÷1-1 \div 1−1÷1.

    You chose D: Solves the real system correctly but attaches the two values to the wrong unknowns.

    Expand the left side, spending i2=−1i^2 = -1i2=−1, and then match parts, which is legitimate because xxx and yyy are real.

    (x+yi)(1+i)=(x−y)+(x+y)i=5−i(x + yi)(1 + i) = (x - y) + (x + y)i = 5 - i(x+yi)(1+i)=(x−y)+(x+y)i=5−i

    So x−y=5x - y = 5x−y=5 and x+y=−1x + y = -1x+y=−1, giving x=2x = 2x=2 and y=−3y = -3y=−3. The check is one multiplication: (2−3i)(1+i)=2+2i−3i+3=5−i(2 - 3i)(1 + i) = 2 + 2i - 3i + 3 = 5 - i(2−3i)(1+i)=2+2i−3i+3=5−i.

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    ∣2−6i∣=40=210,∣9+3i∣=90=310,∣zw∣=210⋅310=60|2 - 6i| = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}, \qquad |9 + 3i| = \sqrt{90} = 3\sqrt{10}, \qquad |zw| = 2\sqrt{10} \cdot 3\sqrt{10} = 60∣2−6i∣=40​=210​,∣9+3i∣=90​=310​,∣zw∣=210​⋅310​=60

    The slow route agrees: (2−6i)(9+3i)=36−48i(2 - 6i)(9 + 3i) = 36 - 48i(2−6i)(9+3i)=36−48i, and 362+482=3600=60\sqrt{36^2 + 48^2} = \sqrt{3600} = 60362+482​=3600​=60.

    Two complex numbers satisfy ∣z∣=6|z| = 6∣z∣=6 and ∣w∣=10|w| = 10∣w∣=10. Which value is IMPOSSIBLE for ∣z+w∣|z + w|∣z+w∣?

    Answer choices for question 17

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Treats the lower end of the window as unreachable, though opposite arrows attain it.

    You chose B: Reads the two bounds as the only permitted values rather than as the ends of a range.

    You chose D: Treats the upper end as unreachable, though arrows pointing the same way attain it.

    The triangle inequality bounds the sum above, and its reverse reading bounds it below, so the length of the sum is confined to a window.

    ∣∣z∣−∣w∣∣≤∣z+w∣≤∣z∣+∣w∣⟹4≤∣z+w∣≤16\bigl||z| - |w|\bigr| \le |z + w| \le |z| + |w| \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 4 \le |z + w| \le 16​∣z∣−∣w∣​≤∣z+w∣≤∣z∣+∣w∣⟹4≤∣z+w∣≤16

    Both ends are attained, by z=6z = 6z=6 with w=−10w = -10w=−10 and by z=6z = 6z=6 with w=10w = 10w=10, and every value between them is available too. Only 202020 lies outside.

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    The equation 5x2+bx+20=05x^2 + bx + 20 = 05x2+bx+20=0 has real bbb and a pair of non-real roots. How far is each root from 000 in the complex plane?

    Answer choices for question 20

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Reports the product of the roots, which is the SQUARE of the distance.

    You chose C: Uses ccc alone as the squared distance, ignoring the leading coefficient.

    You chose D: Assumes the distance needs both coefficients, when the product of the roots already fixes it.

    For a non-real pair p±qip \pm qip±qi the product of the roots is p2+q2p^2 + q^2p2+q2, which is the squared modulus of either one, and the product is also ca\tfrac{c}{a}ac​.

    r1r2=ca=205=4=∣z∣2⟹∣z∣=2r_1 r_2 = \frac{c}{a} = \frac{20}{5} = 4 = |z|^2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad |z| = 2r1​r2​=ac​=520​=4=∣z∣2⟹∣z∣=2

    Every admissible bbb moves the pair along the circle of radius 222 about 000 without changing that distance.

Then give the value of i+i2+⋯+iNi + i^2 + \cdots + i^Ni+i2+⋯+iN for each of the four possibilities for NNN, and say how you know the four possibilities cover every NNN.

      Explain why it works A sentence or two. Reasons, not steps. 5 points

    The answer

    Part A

    i95=−ii^{95} = -ii95=−i and i40=1i^{40} = 1i40=1.

    • i95=−ii^{95} = -ii95=−i may be written 0−1i0 - 1i0−1i; what is not the same is iii, which is the value at remainder 111

    Part B

    The sum is −1-1−1.

    • −1-1−1 may be written −1+0i-1 + 0i−1+0i; an answer of 000 has discarded a block that was never complete

    Part C

    Four consecutive powers factor as ik(1+i+i2+i3)i^k\left(1 + i + i^2 + i^3\right)ik(1+i+i2+i3), and the bracket is 000, so the block vanishes whatever kkk is. What survives is the leftover part of a block, so by the remainder of NNN on division by 444 the sum is 000, iii, i−1i - 1i−1 or −1-1−1.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Divide each exponent by 444 and keep the remainder, since in=iri^n = i^rin=ir whenever n=4q+rn = 4q + rn=4q+r.

    95=4×23+3 ⇒ i95=i3=−i,40=4×10+0 ⇒ i40=i0=195 = 4 \times 23 + 3 \ \Rightarrow\ i^{95} = i^3 = -i, \qquad 40 = 4 \times 10 + 0 \ \Rightarrow\ i^{40} = i^0 = 195=4×23+3 ⇒ i95=i3=−i,40=4×10+0 ⇒ i40=i0=1

    A remainder of 000 means the exponent is a multiple of 444, and (i4)10=110=1\left(i^4\right)^{10} = 1^{10} = 1(i4)10=110=1.

    Part B

    Take the terms in consecutive blocks of four. Each block is a power of iii times 1+i+i2+i31 + i + i^2 + i^31+i+i2+i3, and that bracket is 000.

    1+i+i2+i3=1+i−1−i=01 + i + i^2 + i^3 = 1 + i - 1 - i = 01+i+i2+i3=1+i−1−i=0

    The terms i1i^1i1 through i92i^{92}i92 form 232323 complete blocks and contribute nothing, leaving three terms. Since 93=4×23+193 = 4 \times 23 + 193=4×23+1, those are iii, −1-1−1 and −i-i−i:

    i93+i94+i95=i−1−i=−1i^{93} + i^{94} + i^{95} = i - 1 - i = -1i93+i94+i95=i−1−i=−1

    Part C

    Why a block vanishes. Four consecutive powers starting at ik+1i^{k+1}ik+1 share the factor iki^kik:

    ik+1+ik+2+ik+3+ik+4=ik(i+i2+i3+i4)=ik(i−1−i+1)=ik⋅0=0.i^{k+1} + i^{k+2} + i^{k+3} + i^{k+4} = i^k\left(i + i^2 + i^3 + i^4\right) = i^k(i - 1 - i + 1) = i^k \cdot 0 = 0.ik+1+ik+2+ik+3+ik+4=ik(i+i2+i3+i4)=ik(i−1−i+1)=ik⋅0=0.

    The argument never used the value of kkk, so it covers every starting exponent.

    The four values. Write N=4q+rN = 4q + rN=4q+r with rrr one of 0,1,2,30, 1, 2, 30,1,2,3. The first 4q4q4q terms fall into qqq complete blocks and contribute 000, so the whole sum equals the total of the first rrr terms of the next block, and there are only four of those totals:

    r=0: 0,r=1: i,r=2: i−1,r=3: −1.r = 0: \ 0, \qquad r = 1: \ i, \qquad r = 2: \ i - 1, \qquad r = 3: \ -1.r=0: 0,r=1: i,r=2: i−1,r=3: −1.

    So the running sum only ever takes one of those four values, whatever NNN is. Nothing is left out because dividing by 444 hands every positive integer exactly one of those four remainders.

    In one line

    i95=−ii^{95} = -ii95=−i and i40=1i^{40} = 1i40=1; the sum i+i2+⋯+i95i + i^2 + \cdots + i^{95}i+i2+⋯+i95 is −1-1−1. Any four consecutive powers factor as ik(1+i+i2+i3)=0i^k\left(1 + i + i^2 + i^3\right) = 0ik(1+i+i2+i3)=0, so all that survives a running sum i+⋯+iNi + \cdots + i^Ni+⋯+iN is the leftover part of a block: by the remainder of NNN on division by 444, the value is 000, iii, i−1i - 1i−1 or −1-1−1, and those four remainders cover every NNN.

    For each real number ttt the expression (2+ti)2(2 + ti)^2(2+ti)2 names a complex number, and the whole family is described by two real expressions in ttt: one for the real part and one for the imaginary part. Which members are real and which are pure imaginary is settled by those two slots and nothing else.

      Part A.

      Part C.

      A classmate reads part B and concludes that the square of a non-real number is never real. Decide whether that general claim is true, and settle your decision with a specific number.

      Construct a counterexample Give one specific case, and show it breaks the claim. 5 points

    The answer

    Part A

    (2+ti)2=(4−t2)+4t i(2 + ti)^2 = \left(4 - t^2\right) + 4t\,i(2+ti)2=(4−t2)+4ti, so a=4−t2a = 4 - t^2a=4−t2 and b=4tb = 4tb=4t.

    • 4−t2+4ti4 - t^2 + 4ti4−t2+4ti is the same expression unbracketed; 4+t2+4ti4 + t^2 + 4ti4+t2+4ti is not, since t2i2t^2i^2t2i2 contributes with its sign flipped

    Part B

    Real only at t=0t = 0t=0, where the square is 444. Pure imaginary at t=2t = 2t=2 and t=−2t = -2t=−2, where the square is 8i8i8i and −8i-8i−8i.

    • t=±2t = \pm 2t=±2 names the same two values as t=2t = 2t=2 and t=−2t = -2t=−2; reporting t=0t = 0t=0 as pure imaginary is not the same, since 444 has imaginary part 000

    Part C

    The claim is false. The number 4i4i4i is not real, yet (4i)2=16i2=−16(4i)^2 = 16i^2 = -16(4i)2=16i2=−16, which is real. Part B only ever ranged over the family 2+ti2 + ti2+ti, so it cannot settle a claim about all complex numbers.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Expand as an ordinary square and then exchange i2i^2i2 for −1-1−1, which moves the last term into the real part with its sign flipped.

    (2+ti)2=4+4ti+t2i2=(4−t2)+4t i(2 + ti)^2 = 4 + 4ti + t^2i^2 = \left(4 - t^2\right) + 4t\,i(2+ti)2=4+4ti+t2i2=(4−t2)+4ti

    Both 4−t24 - t^24−t2 and 4t4t4t are real numbers for every real ttt, so this really is standard form.

    Part B

    A complex number is real when its imaginary part is 000, and pure imaginary when its real part is 000 while the imaginary part is not.

    b=4t=0 ⟹ t=0,a=4−t2=0 ⟹ t=±2b = 4t = 0 \ \Longrightarrow\ t = 0, \qquad a = 4 - t^2 = 0 \ \Longrightarrow\ t = \pm 2b=4t=0 ⟹ t=0,a=4−t2=0 ⟹ t=±2

    At t=0t = 0t=0 the square is 444, a real number. At t=2t = 2t=2 it is 8i8i8i and at t=−2t = -2t=−2 it is −8i-8i−8i, and in both cases the imaginary part 4t4t4t is nonzero, so both really are pure imaginary.

    Part C

    The claim is false, and one number refutes it. Take z=4iz = 4iz=4i, whose imaginary part is 4≠04 \ne 04=0, so zzz is not real:

    (4i)2=42i2=16(−1)=−16.(4i)^2 = 4^2 i^2 = 16(-1) = -16.(4i)2=42i2=16(−1)=−16.

    The square is a real number, so a non-real number can certainly have a real square.

    What went wrong in the reasoning is the range of the evidence. Part B searched one family, the numbers 2+ti2 + ti2+ti with real part fixed at 222, and inside that family the only real square did come from t=0t = 0t=0. A statement about every complex number cannot be established by a family that leaves most of them out, and 4i4i4i is one of the numbers left out.

    In one line

    (2+ti)2=(4−t2)+4t i(2 + ti)^2 = \left(4 - t^2\right) + 4t\,i(2+ti)2=(4−t2)+4ti. It is real only at t=0t = 0t=0, where it equals 444, and pure imaginary at t=±2t = \pm 2t=±2, where it equals ±8i\pm 8i±8i. The general claim that a non-real number never has a real square is false: 4i4i4i is not real and (4i)2=−16(4i)^2 = -16(4i)2=−16 is.

      Part A.

      Part C.

      Explain why it works A sentence or two. Reasons, not steps. 6 points

    The answer

    Part A

    1−5i1 - 5i1−5i.

    • 13−65i13\frac{13 - 65i}{13}1313−65i​ is the same value before dividing each part by 131313, so it is unfinished rather than wrong

    Part B

    13+2i=313−213i\dfrac{1}{3 + 2i} = \dfrac{3}{13} - \dfrac{2}{13}i3+2i1​=133​−132​i, and multiplying it by 3+2i3 + 2i3+2i gives 111.

    • 3−2i13\frac{3 - 2i}{13}133−2i​ is the same number with the division left undone across the parts

    Part C

    Multiplying by c−dic−di\frac{c - di}{c - di}c−dic−di​ is multiplying by 111, so the value is unchanged, and the new denominator (c+di)(c−di)=c2+d2(c + di)(c - di) = c^2 + d^2(c+di)(c−di)=c2+d2 is real, which is what makes the parts separable. A sum of two real squares is 000 only when both are 000, so the denominator vanishes only for the divisor 000.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the DENOMINATOR, which is multiplying by 111. The denominator becomes 32+22=133^2 + 2^2 = 1332+22=13, a real number.

    13−13i3+2i=(13−13i)(3−2i)13=39−26i−39i+26i213=13−65i13=1−5i\frac{13 - 13i}{3 + 2i} = \frac{(13 - 13i)(3 - 2i)}{13} = \frac{39 - 26i - 39i + 26i^2}{13} = \frac{13 - 65i}{13} = 1 - 5i3+2i13−13i​=13(13−13i)(3−2i)​=1339−26i−39i+26i2​=1313−65i​=1−5i

    Check by multiplying back: (1−5i)(3+2i)=3+2i−15i+10=13−13i(1 - 5i)(3 + 2i) = 3 + 2i - 15i + 10 = 13 - 13i(1−5i)(3+2i)=3+2i−15i+10=13−13i.

    Part B

    The same move with 111 on top gives the reciprocal directly.

    13+2i=3−2i(3+2i)(3−2i)=3−2i13=313−213i\frac{1}{3 + 2i} = \frac{3 - 2i}{(3 + 2i)(3 - 2i)} = \frac{3 - 2i}{13} = \frac{3}{13} - \frac{2}{13}i3+2i1​=(3+2i)(3−2i)3−2i​=133−2i​=133​−132​i

    The verification is one product, and the conjugate product does the work again:

    (3+2i)⋅3−2i13=32+2213=1313=1.(3 + 2i)\cdot\frac{3 - 2i}{13} = \frac{3^2 + 2^2}{13} = \frac{13}{13} = 1.(3+2i)⋅133−2i​=1332+22​=1313​=1.

    Part C

    Why the conjugate. The fraction c−dic−di\frac{c - di}{c - di}c−dic−di​ is 111 for any nonzero c+dic + dic+di, so multiplying by it changes the costume and not the value. What it buys is that the new denominator is a conjugate product, and the cross terms cancel while i2i^2i2 turns the subtracted square into an added one:

    (c+di)(c−di)=c2−d2i2=c2+d2.(c + di)(c - di) = c^2 - d^2i^2 = c^2 + d^2.(c+di)(c−di)=c2−d2i2=c2+d2.

    That is a real number, and dividing a complex number by a real number is done part by part, which is exactly what standard form requires.

    Why it never fails. Both c2c^2c2 and d2d^2d2 are squares of real numbers, so neither is negative and their sum is 000 only when both are 000, that is only when c=d=0c = d = 0c=d=0. So the only divisor this procedure cannot handle is 000 itself, the same single exception the real numbers always carried.

    In one line

The denominator's conjugate works because c−dic−di\frac{c - di}{c - di}c−dic−di​ is 111 and (c+di)(c−di)=c2+d2(c + di)(c - di) = c^2 + d^2(c+di)(c−di)=c2+d2 is real, and that sum of two real squares is zero only when the divisor is 000.

      Part B.

    The answer

    Part A

    z+w=24+12iz + w = 24 + 12iz+w=24+12i and z−w=2−4iz - w = 2 - 4iz−w=2−4i; ∣z∣=185|z| = \sqrt{185}∣z∣=185​ and ∣w∣=185|w| = \sqrt{185}∣w∣=185​, so the two moduli are equal and the two arrows are the same length.

    The diagonal from 000 has length ∣z+w∣=720|z + w| = \sqrt{720}∣z+w∣=720​; the diagonal joining www and zzz has length ∣z−w∣=20|z - w| = \sqrt{20}∣z−w∣=20​. The first is longer, because 720>20720 > 20720>20 and both lengths are non-negative.

    • 720=125\sqrt{720} = 12\sqrt{5}720​=125​ and 20=25\sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}20​=25​ are the same two lengths simplified; comparing 720720720 with 202020 is the same comparison as comparing the roots, since both are non-negative

    Part C

    The first half holds: opposite sides are copies of the arrows for zzz and www, so equal moduli make all four sides equal. The second half fails, and part B refutes it, 720\sqrt{720}720​ against 20\sqrt{20}20​. Equal sides fix how far each arrow reaches, not how the two are placed, and the diagonals depend on the placement.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Combine the parts separately for the sum and the difference, distributing the minus sign through both parts of www.

    z+w=(13+11)+(4+8)i=24+12i,z−w=(13−11)+(4−8)i=2−4iz + w = (13 + 11) + (4 + 8)i = 24 + 12i, \qquad z - w = (13 - 11) + (4 - 8)i = 2 - 4iz+w=(13+11)+(4+8)i=24+12i,z−w=(13−11)+(4−8)i=2−4i

    Each modulus is a Pythagorean computation, and the two happen to agree:

    ∣z∣=169+16=185,∣w∣=121+64=185.|z| = \sqrt{169 + 16} = \sqrt{185}, \qquad |w| = \sqrt{121 + 64} = \sqrt{185}.∣z∣=169+16​=185​,∣w∣=121+64​=185​.

    Part B

    The gap between two complex numbers is the modulus of their difference, so the second diagonal has length ∣z−w∣|z - w|∣z−w∣, while the first runs from 000 and has length ∣z+w∣|z + w|∣z+w∣.

    ∣z+w∣=242+122=720=125,∣z−w∣=22+(−4)2=20=25|z + w| = \sqrt{24^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{720} = 12\sqrt{5}, \qquad |z - w| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}∣z+w∣=242+122​=720​=125​,∣z−w∣=22+(−4)2​=20​=25​

    No decimals are needed for the comparison: both numbers are non-negative, so the one with the larger square is the larger number, and 720>20720 > 20720>20.

    Part C

    The first half is sound. The four sides are translated copies of the arrows for zzz and for www, two of each, and translation does not change length. So the sides have lengths ∣z∣|z|∣z∣, ∣w∣|w|∣w∣, ∣z∣|z|∣z∣, ∣w∣|w|∣w∣, and ∣z∣=∣w∣=185|z| = |w| = \sqrt{185}∣z∣=∣w∣=185​ makes all four equal.

    The second half is false, and part B already refutes it:

    ∣z+w∣=720≠20=∣z−w∣.|z + w| = \sqrt{720} \ne \sqrt{20} = |z - w|.∣z+w∣=720​=20​=∣z−w∣.

    What the moduli record is how far each arrow reaches from 000, and nothing about the direction it reaches in. The diagonals are built from the sum and the difference, and those depend on how the two arrows are placed relative to each other. Two arrows of equal length can be nearly aligned, making ∣z+w∣|z + w|∣z+w∣ nearly 2∣z∣2|z|2∣z∣ and ∣z−w∣|z - w|∣z−w∣ nearly 000, or nearly opposite, which reverses the two. Here they are nearly aligned: the triangle inequality caps the long diagonal at ∣z∣+∣w∣=2185=740|z| + |w| = 2\sqrt{185} = \sqrt{740}∣z∣+∣w∣=2185​=740​, and 720\sqrt{720}720​ sits just under it.

    In one line

    z+w=24+12iz + w = 24 + 12iz+w=24+12i, z−w=2−4iz - w = 2 - 4iz−w=2−4i, and ∣z∣=∣w∣=185|z| = |w| = \sqrt{185}∣z∣=∣w∣=185​, so all four sides are equal. The diagonals are ∣z+w∣=720=125|z + w| = \sqrt{720} = 12\sqrt{5}∣z+w∣=720​=125​ and ∣z−w∣=20=25|z - w| = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}∣z−w∣=20​=25​, and the first is longer because 720>20720 > 20720>20. Equal sides therefore do not force equal diagonals: a modulus records how far an arrow reaches, not how the two arrows are placed relative to each other.

    The equation becomes a2+b2=(a−6)2+b2a^2 + b^2 = (a - 6)^2 + b^2a2+b2=(a−6)2+b2, which simplifies to 12a=3612a = 3612a=36, that is a=3a = 3a=3. No condition on bbb survives.

    • a=3a = 3a=3 is the whole content; a=3a = 3a=3 together with any restriction on bbb is not, since bbb cancels completely

    Part B

    It is the vertical line of all numbers with real part 333, the mirror line midway between 000 and 666. Two members are 333 and 3+4i3 + 4i3+4i; for the second, ∣3+4i∣=5|3 + 4i| = 5∣3+4i∣=5 and ∣3+4i−6∣=∣−3+4i∣=5|3 + 4i - 6| = |-3 + 4i| = 5∣3+4i−6∣=∣−3+4i∣=5.

    • The line may be named as the numbers 3+bi3 + bi3+bi with bbb real, or as the perpendicular bisector of the segment from 000 to 666

    Part C

    The objection fails. A circle needs ∣z−c∣=r|z - c| = r∣z−c∣=r with rrr a positive constant. Here both sides carry zzz with coefficient 111, so squaring cancels a2a^2a2 and b2b^2b2 and leaves a linear equation, whose solutions form a line. Replacing one side by a positive constant, as in ∣z−6∣=4|z - 6| = 4∣z−6∣=4, restores the squared terms and with them the circle.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Both distances are moduli, so square both sides, which is safe because both are non-negative.

    ∣a+bi∣2=∣(a−6)+bi∣2 ⟹ a2+b2=(a−6)2+b2|a + bi|^2 = |(a - 6) + bi|^2 \ \Longrightarrow\ a^2 + b^2 = (a - 6)^2 + b^2∣a+bi∣2=∣(a−6)+bi∣2 ⟹ a2+b2=(a−6)2+b2

    The b2b^2b2 terms are identical on the two sides and cancel, and so does a2a^2a2 once the right side is expanded:

    a2+b2=a2−12a+36+b2 ⟹ 0=−12a+36 ⟹ a=3.a^2 + b^2 = a^2 - 12a + 36 + b^2 \ \Longrightarrow\ 0 = -12a + 36 \ \Longrightarrow\ a = 3.a2+b2=a2−12a+36+b2 ⟹ 0=−12a+36 ⟹ a=3.

    Every squared term has gone, leaving one linear equation in aaa and no condition at all on bbb.

    Part B

    The condition a=3a = 3a=3 with bbb free describes every number of the form 3+bi3 + bi3+bi: a vertical line in the plane, crossing the real axis at 333, which is the midpoint of 000 and 666.

    Take z=3z = 3z=3 and z=3+4iz = 3 + 4iz=3+4i. The check on the second is two modulus computations:

    ∣3+4i∣=9+16=5,∣(3+4i)−6∣=∣−3+4i∣=9+16=5.|3 + 4i| = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5, \qquad |(3 + 4i) - 6| = |-3 + 4i| = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5.∣3+4i∣=9+16​=5,∣(3+4i)−6∣=∣−3+4i∣=9+16​=5.

    The two distances agree, as the equation demands. The picture makes the answer unsurprising: the numbers equally far from two fixed points are exactly the numbers on the line that cuts the segment between them in half at a right angle.

    Part C

    The objection has no force as stated. What produces a circle is an equation of the form ∣z−c∣=r|z - c| = r∣z−c∣=r in which one side is a fixed POSITIVE number: squaring then gives (a−p)2+(b−q)2=r2(a - p)^2 + (b - q)^2 = r^2(a−p)2+(b−q)2=r2, and the squared terms are what bend the picture.

    Why this one comes out straight. Here zzz sits inside the modulus on both sides, and on each side it carries coefficient 111, so both sides produce the same a2+b2a^2 + b^2a2+b2 and squaring destroys exactly those terms:

    a2+b2=(a−6)2+b2 ⟹ 12a=36.a^2 + b^2 = (a - 6)^2 + b^2 \ \Longrightarrow\ 12a = 36.a2+b2=(a−6)2+b2 ⟹ 12a=36.

    What is left is linear in aaa and bbb, and a linear equation in the two coordinates describes a line. The geometry says the same thing: the equation asks for the points that cannot tell 000 from 666, and those are the points of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them.

    What would restore a circle. Fix the right side as a positive constant. The equation ∣z−6∣=4|z - 6| = 4∣z−6∣=4 keeps its squared terms, and its solution set is the circle of radius 444 about 666. A modulus equation gives a circle when one side depends on zzz and the other is a positive constant; put 000 on the right and the solution set shrinks to a single point, and put a negative number there and nothing satisfies it at all.

    In one line

    Writing z=a+biz = a + biz=a+bi turns ∣z∣=∣z−6∣|z| = |z - 6|∣z∣=∣z−6∣ into a2+b2=(a−6)2+b2a^2 + b^2 = (a - 6)^2 + b^2a2+b2=(a−6)2+b2, which collapses to a=3a = 3a=3 with bbb free: the vertical line of numbers 3+bi3 + bi3+bi, the perpendicular bisector of the segment from 000 to 666, containing 333 and 3+4i3 + 4i3+4i. It is a line rather than a circle because both sides carry zzz with coefficient 111, so squaring cancels a2a^2a2 and b2b^2b2 and leaves a linear equation; an equation such as ∣z−6∣=4|z - 6| = 4∣z−6∣=4, whose right side is a positive constant, keeps its squared terms and gives a circle.
